> for the selected Love Burn proposal. Dimensions, depicted equipment, LED
> allocations and delivery status below describe that earlier study; they are

# Packing, installation, operation and strike

## Before loading

1. Freeze one option/module revision and print its approved drawings, manuals,
   contact details, inventory and operating limits. Keep budget/approval receipts together.
2. Check each serialized lifting/electrical/optical item and its inspection status;
   segregate damaged or unidentified pieces. Pack the accepted repair kit separately.
3. Mark triangle front/rear and matching joints; bag retainers by assembly and
   label cases CORE, LANDER, OPTICS, CAPTURE, HAZE, RIGGING, OPERATIONS.
4. Record quantities, mass, dimensions and vehicle loading/securement plan from
   actual equipment. The truck is transport only; do not infer capacity from the model.
5. Confirm all borrowed items, return dates and assigned crew; photograph the packed kit.

## At the site

1. Confirm the approved position, underground/overhead restrictions, access,
   surface and power with placement before unloading the full installation.
2. Mark the complete footprint including arms, host, ballast and circulation;
   place the entrance-facing open bay first. Keep the approach free throughout setup.
3. Unload into a controlled work area; assemble the accepted base/host and ground
   protection according to its drawing/manual. Do not improvise stakes or tree ties.
4. Install sphere/support empty, then optics/covers/cables, checking final mass
   and balance. Route power at the rear/sides with appropriate protection.
5. Complete commissioning: electrical protection, inflation/ventilation,
   contact/clearance, show/blackout, communication, retrieval and weather limits.
6. Release occupied operation only after the required review/venue checks and
   a fully staffed rehearsal; record who has stop authority.

## Each operating session

1. Operator checks weather and actual assembly against the released revision;
   inspect inflation, contact zones, joints, legs/footing or rigging, cords and covers.
2. Spotter clears the entrance and verifies the stop/communication/retrieval method.
3. Explain participation, consent for any camera feed and immediate exit; use
   only the occupancy and conditions permitted by the selected system.
4. Monitor participant comfort, equipment temperature, inflation and conditions;
   close immediately at the approved stop criteria or any unexpected behaviour.
5. End the session using the approved ground/lowering procedure; isolate power,
   cool effects equipment and record defects before the next opening.

Do not improvise numerical wind limits, occupancy times, ballast weights or
proof-test loads. Those are outputs of the actual equipment/design review.

## Strike and return

1. Close participation, evacuate through the approved procedure, isolate effects
   and lower/support the apparatus by the accepted method.
2. Deflate, disassemble and protect surfaces following product instructions;
   keep heavy/dirty metal away from the sphere and lenses.
3. Count every part and fastener; sweep the site for tape, metal, plastic, fluid
   residue and other material, then obtain the agreed site handback.
4. Dry, clean, inspect and quarantine damage; record actual consumption and costs.
5. Return loans and update Pacinman custody, condition and task completion.
